requirement: The requirements index MUST list examples as well as requirements, identify each entry's kind, and show each example's evidence state. Example detail pages and their links MUST follow {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages` and {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; references to an example MUST link to its definition.
rationale:
The marked tests cover every obligation in `requirements.examples.index`.

**Index lists examples and requirements, and identifies each entry's kind.**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages]` asserts index rows of the form `| [`rules.pending`](requirements-index/rules.pending.html) (example)`.
- It asserts the same for `rules.missing`, and a `(requirement)` row for `rules.ready`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` asserts `(requirement)` and `(example)` appear in the default index.

**Index shows each example's evidence state.**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_and_detail_pages_show_each_example_evidence_state]` builds five examples: valid, pending, FIXME, changed text, and missing.
- For each, it parses the row's state column and asserts exactly `Recorded true`, `Recorded false`, `Recorded FIXME`, `Recorded true` (the changed case), and `Missing`.
- It also asserts the detail page's badge alt text carries the same state.
- `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book]` checks FIXME in the index and detail page.

**Example detail pages follow `requirements.index.detail_pages`.**
- Example pages exist as subchapters of the index, in definition order. `src/lib.rs` `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` asserts the names `rules.zeta`, `rules.alpha`, `rules.cli.mdbook`, `rules.child.nested`.
- The same test asserts each page's parent and section number, so the example `rules.alpha` is covered.
- The pages are titled by full name (`rules.pending` and `rules.missing` in the `src/index.rs` test).

**Links follow `requirements.index.navigation`.**
- Example definition badges have an anchored `id`/`href` pair, asserted in `index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages` and `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages`.
- Each detail page links back to the index via `[Requirements index](../requirements-index.html)`.
- Each detail page links back to the definition via `[View definition](...#habeas-example-...)`.
- There is no "See evidence" plaintext link, and the arrow icon `habeas-detail-icon` is present.
- A `.md`-containing name is covered for a requirement, and `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` in `src/lib.rs` covers an example named `more.cli.mdbook`. I read only its matched snippets, and that test carries no `requirements.examples.index` marker in the supplied inputs. I did not need it for this judgment.

**References to an example link to its definition.** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` asserts that a `{test}` reference to `requirements.something.foo` renders as `href="../requirements.html#habeas-example-requirements.something.foo"`.

The detailed link, icon-styling and `.md` mechanics are the cited requirements' own obligations. The subject only needs them applied to examples, and the tests show that.

I found no obligation without a test and no untested failure case.

text: The requirements index MUST list examples as well as requirements, identify each entry's kind, and show each example's evidence state. Example detail pages and their links MUST follow {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages` and {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; references to an example MUST link to its definition.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its own anchored definition on the current page. The badge MUST have a separate adjacent link containing an accessible right-arrow icon in an integrated segment matching the badge color linking to its evidence detail page. The badge and arrow MUST remain aligned in one non-wrapping row. Definitions MUST NOT be followed by a separate plaintext evidence link. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
